title: Viva Engage: enhanced Microsoft Copilot with Engage tools, work context and agents
summary: Hold: the cost rating and rationale describe indirect costs only, although the Cowork route covered by this briefing has documented usage-based billing. The roadmap facts, automatic activation, licence-removal control and both API operations are supported; the plugin path and a few source and governance qualifications need small corrections.

claims.claim: The assignLicense request body's removeLicenses property specifies the licences to remove.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Removing the Microsoft Copilot licence is not Engage-specific and removes the user's wider Copilot access.

claims.claim: The package block API is a Microsoft Graph beta operation.

claims.claim: The low cost rating and rationale say the only direct cost is admin time and communications despite including Cowork tasks in scope.
claims.quote: Page: 'the direct cost is admin time and communications.' Microsoft: 'Cowork uses a usage-based billing model. Activities such as model responses, tool and skill calls, image generation, and browser tasks count toward your organization's consumption.'
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable'. Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. The Copilot pane requires a Microsoft Copilot licence; Cowork tasks accessed from it use usage-based billing measured in Copilot Credits. Allow for admin time and communications.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/cowork/cowork-admin-governance and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits, and add to Cost and licensing: 'Cowork tasks consume Copilot Credits; model responses and tool and skill calls count toward consumption.' Keep licensing.model 'included' for entitlement to the enhanced pane.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review private-community membership and posting permissions and Purview audit logs, but neither control appears in the table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review membership and posting permissions in private communities' and 'Review Microsoft Purview audit logs'. Table: licence assignment, separate Engage-switch absence, and Cowork plugin availability only.
claims.fix: The private-community membership/posting-permission review and Purview audit review steps have no matching control rows. Remove those two checklist bullets to align the checklist with the existing table; do not add unverified rows.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph; controls[2].api applicability
claims.claim: The package block operation is a general control, but the page leaves its coverage of the Engage plugin as something to confirm in the tenant.
claims.quote: A package represents an agent or a tool, such as a plugin, MCP server, or skill, in the organization catalog. Admin blocks a package to prevent its usage across the organization.
claims.fix: Replace 'whether the Engage plugin appears as a package for this call is something to confirm in your tenant' with 'the Package Management API covers agents and tools, including plugins, in the organization catalog'. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/overview to sources. Keep the existing beta call and Agent 365 licence qualification.
